strategy.title: Six signed album-mix packages, mixed by Hollow Tree Mixing
strategy.why: Six studio owners signed $1,200 orders (written acceptances); Hollow Tree Mixing quoted $540 a package and can deliver all six by day 21. reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is right. cop_574ab6e4a6fa4fc0adb8 has six WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE orders at $1,200 (a price these studios signed), a recorded fulfiller Hollow Tree Mixing that performs the delivery ($540 a package, 2 a week on days 7, 14, 21 = 6 by day 21, invoiced net 7), and studio payment on delivery cleared 3 days later. Every link is established on the card. Arithmetic recomputed against the CONTRIBUTION metric: 6 x ($1,200 - $540) = 6 x $660 = $3,960 >= $3,000 kept after all direct costs. Every mixer invoice ($1,080 on days 14, 21, 28) falls inside the 35-day window and is paid from receipts that cleared on days 10, 17 and 24, so cash never goes negative (min $0), no capital is advanced and exposure stays at the $0 cap. Five packages ($3,300) would still clear the target, so one slipped order does not break it. Excluding the lacquer cutting is correct: Groove Lane's $380 cost is above the $350 signed price, so each side loses $30 and adding it only lowers contribution.
findings: proofDay is recorded as 10, but at day 10 only $2,400 has cleared with $3,240 of mixer cost still to come; contribution is $3,960 net of every cost only once the day-24 receipts clear (and final after the day-28 payment). The proof day should be 24-28; this does not change the stance.
Only the six signed studios are the market (no buyer volume beyond them), which is fine because the plan sells nothing beyond the signed orders.
